description:
Runs Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI and other terminal coding agents together on one mission.

Runner is a native desktop application where terminal agents work together. Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Cursor CLI, Grok Build, Antigravity CLI, Copilot CLI and pi can take the same task in one mission, and each agent keeps its own TUI in a real terminal while the lead brings the decisions back to you. Everything in Runner is also a `runner` command: missions, crews, roles, projects, chats, sessions and messages are all addressable from the command line, with `runnerd` as the background service. Agents run natively on Windows without WSL, and PowerShell 7 is optional. Status: alpha, actively shipping. Native builds target macOS (Apple Silicon) and Windows (x64) on Windows 10 version 1809 or later; Intel Macs, Windows ARM64 and Linux are not supported. The installer, the application and the CLI sidecars are Authenticode-signed with a Certum open-source certificate issued to Open Source Developer Yicheng Wang.
Runner 0.16.8 is a feature release for macOS and Windows on top of 0.16.7.
New
- A scrollbar on the mission feed. The feed now shows the same scrollbar as the sidebar and Settings, so you can see where you are in a long mission and drag to another point. (#947)
- Clearer inbox reads for agents. When an agent reads messages with runner msg read --since or --from and unread messages remain, the CLI now says how many are still unread and how to clear them with a plain runner msg read. Agent guidance and the guide explain the difference. (#965)
Bug fixes
- Long mission feeds stay responsive. Scrolling, typing in the feed composer and new events no longer slow down as a mission's feed grows, including very long posts and long runs of messages from one agent. (#962)
- Restored missions can be resumed. Restoring a mission from Settings → Archived, or with runner mission unarchive, now reopens it: its members stay stopped until you choose Resume, messages work again, and the feed marks the reopen. Before, a restored mission came back to the sidebar but refused to resume. (#890)
- pi members resume their own conversation in symlinked folders. In a mission whose folder is reached through a symbolic link, a pi member that had already worked could lose its conversation on Resume and start over. It now continues where it left off. (#971)
- Active sidebar rows stay in place. Rows in the Active view no longer jump around as agents start, finish, ask for approval or produce new output. Each group keeps its rows in the order they were created, so ⌘1–9 keep pointing at the same rows. (#972)
